summary: Configured persistent public-key-only SSH access for `opsbot` from node1 to node2. Functional access and restart persistence were verified on both nodes.
actions_performed: Generated an ED25519 keypair as `opsbot` on node1 and installed its public key on both systems.
Applied explicit per-user SSH rules requiring public-key authentication and disabling password authentication.
Verified successful `opsbot` SSH access from node1 to node2 and rejection of password-only access.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: `opsbot` exists with matching key material and public-key-only SSH policy on both systems
evidence.summary: Both nodes show UID 1001, matching ED25519 fingerprint, active/enabled SSH, `pubkeyauthentication yes`, `passwordauthentication no`, and `authenticationmethods publickey`.

evidence.requirement: `opsbot` on node1 can run commands as `opsbot` on node2, while password-only authentication is rejected
evidence.summary: Cross-node sessions returned `opsbot@node2` with UID 1001. Password-only attempts failed with `Permission denied (publickey)`, including after both restarts.

Healthy baseline boot ID `fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a`, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID `7e8438ff-5aea-446b-9516-948289590b3b`, then recovered SSH, account, key, policy, self-login, and node2 access.

Healthy baseline boot ID `a59a9d9a-a5e0-44f7-9ca1-7f28483971e0`, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID `723e9aeb-3a38-4de6-8680-b7efa2594094`, then recovered SSH, account, authorized key, policy, and cross-node access.
